meta_review.summary: This paper introduces Modular Expert Paths (MoEP), a novel architecture designed to enhance the efficiency of large language models (LLMs) by incorporating sparsity without increasing the total parameter count. The core idea behind MoEP is to combine model parallelism with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) techniques, employing selective token activation through linear projections and SwiGLU variants. The architecture consists of parallel blocks, each operating at a reduced dimension, interconnected by a top-k routing mechanism. This routing mechanism allows each token to activate only a subset of the parallel blocks, thus creating diverse computational pathways and reducing redundancy. The authors further integrate MoE layers, using either linear projections or SwiGLU feedforward networks, to reduce and then restore the hidden dimension, ensuring compatibility with standard transformer models. The proposed model is evaluated on the BabyLM benchmark, a suite of tasks designed to assess language modeling performance. The empirical results indicate that MoEP achieves marginally better performance compared to a GPT-2 baseline, despite having fewer parameters. The authors emphasize that MoEP demonstrates superior sample efficiency, extracting useful patterns earlier during training. The authors also highlight the potential of their approach to inspire future research in model efficiency by combining parallel processing paths with MoE techniques.
